lesson_evidence.heading: 2. Finding and interpreting eigenvalues
lesson_evidence.exact_excerpt:
A real symmetric matrix has especially useful properties. All its eigenvalues are real, and it has an orthonormal basis of eigenvectors. Thus, for an $n$ by $n$ symmetric matrix, we can write

$$A=Q\Lambda Q^T,$$

where the columns of $Q$ are orthonormal eigenvectors and $\Lambda$ is diagonal with the corresponding eigenvalues.
